name: product-widget
purpose: Draws one of the **official console widgets**: a scaled, inert mock of an Azion Console screen or fragment, built from real webkit components inside a `shell-mockup` frame, that marketing bands use to show the product. `name` selects the widget from a closed registry of 70 drawings, loaded on demand, so a page can only render mocks that already exist and the same screen is the same drawing on every page that shows it. The remaining props pass through to the widget that declares them, and a widget that does not declare one keeps its own value.
useWhen: A product band (hero, media split, feature tab, widget grid cell) needs to show a console screen or a fragment of one.
The same console screen appears on more than one page and must be the same drawing on each.
Several widgets share one slot (tabs), and only the one showing should play: drive `active` from the host.
A grid cell plays its fragment's beat while the pointer is over it: drive `hover` from the host.
avoidWhen: The screen you need is not in the registry → compose it with `shell-mockup` and its parts, then add it to the registry. Do not approximate it at the call site.
A live, working screen at a device size → use `browser-frame`.
A static product concept drawing → use `illustration`.
A screenshot or clip in documentation → use `doc-frame`.
related: shell-mockup` — the frame every widget is drawn in; reach for it directly to compose a new screen.
illustration` — the same closed-registry pattern for static scenes.
texture-material` — the texture a full-screen widget grounds itself with through `texture`.
bestPractices: Give the host a size (a height or an aspect ratio). A widget fills its host and scales its design width to fit.

Host a framed widget (a full screen) in a wide panel, and a fragment in a grid cell with its own padding. Fragments are drawn bare and float on the cell's surface, so set `--mockup-fade-color` on the cell when it is not `--bg-canvas`.
Leave `kind`, `chrome`, `width`, `tab` and `interval` unset unless the host needs a different value: unset keeps the widget's own.
Keep the copy beside the widget saying what it shows. Every widget but `function-code` and the coding-agent switch of `functions-start` is hidden from assistive technology.

props.name: name
props.doc: Name of the console widget to draw.

props.name: active
props.doc: Whether this widget is the one showing; it replays its entrance each time it becomes active.

props.name: hover
props.doc: Whether the pointer is over the host; a fragment plays its beat while it is.

props.name: kind
props.doc: How a framed widget is plated; unset keeps the widget's own plating.

props.name: chrome
props.doc: Draws the console bar on a framed widget; unset keeps the widget's own bar.

props.name: width
props.doc: Design width of a framed widget from md up; unset keeps the widget's own width.

props.name: fade
props.doc: Edge a framed widget fades out along.

props.name: texture
props.doc: Texture a full-screen widget is grounded with.

props.name: tab
props.doc: Tab a tabbed widget plays (`workload-overview`, `application-version`, `functions-start`); other widgets ignore it, and unset plays the first tab.

props.name: interval
props.doc: Milliseconds between revealed log lines in the deploy logs widget; unset keeps its own pace.
